title: French high school students protest conditions, block schools nationwide
seoTitle: France student protests over school conditions

tea.why: Students are protesting staff shortages, dilapidated buildings, under-resourced schools, long hours, overcrowding, and absent teachers.
tea.want: Protesters demand increased resources, better learning conditions, hiring of substitute teachers, and addressing the university application process.
tea.changed: Oct 5: A 15-year-old student lost a hand during a protest in Lens, and the education ministry reported over 400 high schools were partially or totally closed.

summary: High school students across France have been protesting since September 17, blocking hundreds of schools to demand better learning conditions and increased resources. Organizers, including student unions and the CGT labour union, cite grievances such as teacher shortages, overcrowded classrooms, and dilapidated facilities. The demonstrations have led to clashes with police, resulting in hundreds of arrests and injuries. The government has held crisis meetings, with the Prime Minister calling for peaceful gatherings, while the Education Minister announced school closures and accused far-left activists of inciting violence. Further protests are expected, with trade unions joining students.
demands: More chairs in classrooms and longer lunch breaks
response: Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu's office held a crisis meeting and called for peaceful gatherings. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez issued orders for police to break up blockades. updates.text: The protests began at a school in Paris.
Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu's office held a crisis meeting on the protests. A headteacher was attacked and a fire truck was set alight in Marseille.
More than 400 schools remained closed across France. Student representatives called for non-violent protests to continue.
Education Minister Edouard Geffray announced that 400 to 500 high schools would be partially or completely closed on Monday.
A 15-year-old student lost a hand during a protest in Lens. The education ministry reported over 400 high schools were partially or totally closed.
Tens of thousands of demonstrators, including trade unions, are expected to join protests in Paris.
